verdict.rationale: Cooley GO's own Delaware Incorporation Package generator produces a Restricted Stock Purchase Agreement and, when the stock vests, a Section 83(b) election form with escrow instructions, so 83(b) and vesting mechanics are covered by first-party materials. Co-founder equity splits rest only on a community mention of Cooley GO posts about allocating initial founder equity, and vesting-schedule design is implied rather than documented. missing for 10: first-party documentation of co-founder equity-split guidance, explicit vesting-schedule terms and options (e.g., cliff/duration), local-equivalent coverage outside the US 83(b), independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, the firm's own materials cover founder equity mechanics — vesting schedules, 83(b) elections or the local equivalent, and equity splits among co-founders — so day-zero ownership is set up right

citations.quote: If the stock is subject to vesting, the following will be included: Form of Section 83(b) Election; Joint Escrow Instructions; Stock Assignment Separate From Certificate
Restricted Stock Purchase Agreement, which automatically includes an Assignment Agreement for intellectual property
plus posts on FAQs like allocating initial founder equity and equity incentive tax issues
